record.paper_title: Open Problem: Is There an Online Learning Algorithm That Learns Whenever Online Learning Is Possible?
record.context_brief: Strong universal online learning characterization by C_s
record.original_question: In realizable binary online learning with arbitrary measurable target concepts f*: X → {0,1}, say that strong universal online learning is possible under a possibly random instance sequence X if some online learning algorithm has total mistakes o(T) through time T almost surely for every measurable f*. Let C_s be the family of all possibly random sequences X = {X_t}_{t∈N} such that every disjoint sequence {A_i}_{i∈N} of measurable sets satisfies |{i ∈ N : {X_1,...,X_T} intersects A_i}| = o(T) almost surely. Is C_s exactly equal to the set of all instance sequences X such that strong universal online learning is possible under X?

evidence.quote: Definition 1 For a (possibly random) sequence X = {X_t}_{t∈N}, an online learning algorithm f_t : X^{t−1} × {0,1}^{t−1} × X → {0,1} (possibly randomized, independent of X) is strongly universally consistent under X if, for every (measurable) f* : X → {0,1}, ∑_{t=1}^T 1[f_t(X_{1:(t−1)},f*(X_{1:(t−1)}),X_t) ≠ f*(X_t)] = o(T) (a.s.).

Definition 2 For a (possibly random) sequence X, we say (weak/strong) universal online learning is possible under X if there exists an online learning algorithm that is (weakly/strongly) universally consistent under X.
Let C_s denote the family of all (possibly random) sequences X = {X_t}_{t∈N} such that every disjoint sequence {A_i}_{i∈N} of measurable sets satisfies |{i ∈ N : X_{1:T} ∩ A_i ≠ ∅}|= o(T) (a.s.).
Open Problem 2 • Is C_s equal to the set of all X such that strong universal online learning is possible under X?

Thus, the case that remains open in Open Problem 2 concerns whether X ∈ C_w or X ∈ C_s are sufficient conditions for weak or strong, respectively, universal online learning to be possible under X for uncountable X and general (random) sequences X.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a measurable space, and consider realizable binary online learning with arbitrary measurable target concepts $f^*: \mathcal{X} \to \{0,1\}$. A (possibly random) instance sequence is a stochastic process $\mathbf{X} = \{X_t\}_{t \in \mathbb{N}}$ taking values in $\mathcal{X}$. An online learning algorithm is a sequence of (possibly randomized, independent of $\mathbf{X}$) measurable maps $f_t: \mathcal{X}^{t-1} \times \{0,1\}^{t-1} \times \mathcal{X} \to \{0,1\}$. The algorithm is said to be strongly universally consistent under $\mathbf{X}$ if, for every measurable $f^*: \mathcal{X} \to \{0,1\}$,
$$\sum_{t=1}^{T} \mathbf{1}\big[f_t(X_{1:t-1}, f^*(X_{1:t-1}), X_t) \neq f^*(X_t)\big] = o(T) \quad \text{almost surely.}$$
Strong universal online learning is said to be possible under $\mathbf{X}$ if some online learning algorithm is strongly universally consistent under $\mathbf{X}$.

Define $\mathcal{C}_s$ to be the family of all (possibly random) sequences $\mathbf{X} = \{X_t\}_{t \in \mathbb{N}}$ such that, for every disjoint sequence $\{A_i\}_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ of measurable subsets of $\mathcal{X}$,
$$\big|\{i \in \mathbb{N} : \{X_1, \dots, X_T\} \cap A_i \neq \emptyset\}\big| = o(T) \quad \text{almost surely.}$$

Question. Is $\mathcal{C}_s$ exactly equal to the set of all (possibly random) instance sequences $\mathbf{X}$ such that strong universal online learning is possible under $\mathbf{X}$?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Blanchard (and collaborators) — in particular "Universal Online Learning: an Optimistically Universal Learning Rule" (2022) — gives a complete characterization of the processes admitting strong (and weak) universal online learning, and is described as closing all COLT 2021 open problems by Hanneke on universal online learning. The characterizing condition (called SMV / $C_2$) coincides with the proposed family $\mathcal{C}_s$, so $\mathcal{C}_s$ is indeed the exact set of $\mathbf{X}$ admitting strong universal online learning.

status_evidence.title: Universal Online Learning: an Optimistically Universal Learning Rule
status_evidence.snippet: Gives a complete characterization of the processes admitting strong and weak universal learning, closing COLT 2021 open problems posed by Hanneke on universal online learning.
status_evidence.claim: The open problem on whether C_s characterizes processes admitting strong universal online learning has been resolved.

status_evidence.title: A Theory of Optimistically Universal Online Learnability for General Concept Classes
status_evidence.snippet: The works of Blanchard and Cosson (2022); Blanchard et al. (2022a); Blanchard (2022) show that the processes that admit strongly universal online learning satisfy the condition C_2 (=SMV).
status_evidence.claim: Characterization of strongly universal online learning by C_s/SMV is established.
